idea.name: Backyard Funhouse sport courts and amenities
idea.one_liner: Sell sport courts, pools, putting greens, and other backyard amenities to homeowners in greater DFW, using subcontractors to deliver projects.
idea.customer: Homeowners in the greater DFW area.
idea.offer: Sport courts, pools, putting greens, and other backyard amenities.
idea.revenue_model: Project-based sales; actual prices charged by Backyard Funhouse are not stated.

key_quotes.quote: I own a tree trimming business and we recently discovered that we love the sport court business because our tree trimming jobs are about $1,500 on average and a sport court job is about $50 to $60,000 on average.
I just had my own sport court built and I subcontracted out all the work and saved about $25,000 on the job.
So now I have a whole rolodex of subcontractors that I can use to sell sport courts to someone else.

But the new website needs to be for a business called Backyard Funhouse, which is a business that builds sport courts, pools, putting greens, and other fun backyard amenities only within the greater DFW area.
What the ready agent does is takes my caveman language and turns it into a prompt that looks to be perfectly prompt engineered, if you will.

claims.claim: A sport-court job averages about $50,000 to $60,000.
claims.quote: a sport court job is about $50 to $60,000 on average

claims.claim: He says he saved about $25,000 on his own sport-court build by subcontracting the work.
claims.quote: I just had my own sport court built and I subcontracted out all the work and saved about $25,000 on the job.

claims.quote: 5 minutes exactly. That is pretty dang good.

claims.claim: Each photo replacement took about 15 to 20 seconds.
claims.quote: Each one of these photo swaps took about 15 20 seconds.

acquisition_channels.details: Ready is described as optimizing the site for SEO and indexing it with Google.

ideas.delivery: Koerner says he would sell the projects and subcontract the physical work. Ready is used for the website and inbound lead handling.

prices: about $25,000 saved on his own build

idea.name: Website agency
idea.one_liner: Build conversion-focused websites for home-service businesses using Ready, charging project fees, monthly fees, or a combination.
idea.offer: Website creation and optimization, including landing pages, appointment setup, and integrations.
idea.revenue_model: Website project fees and/or monthly fees; the speaker suggests testing prices with prospects.

key_quotes.quote: You could start your own website agency.
Not too long ago, you could charge thousands of dollars to build websites like these.
It could be the difference between getting 10 $50,000 leads a month or 13 $50,000 leads a month.
One flat fee to one guy, 100 bucks a month to another guy, a combo of both to a third guy.

If you look at their integrations, you can integrate with Stripe so you can charge directly on the website, Calendarly to set up appointments, Google Analytics to see what your traffic is, or even Shopify so you can sell physical and or digital products.

claims.claim: The speaker says websites like these could have been charged at thousands of dollars, and says they can still be charged at that level.
claims.quote: Not too long ago, you could charge thousands of dollars to build websites like these.

claims.claim: A highly converting website could be worth millions of dollars a year to a business.
claims.quote: It could be worth millions of dollars a year.

claims.claim: A website could change monthly leads valued at $50,000 each from 10 to 13.
claims.quote: It could be the difference between getting 10 $50,000 leads a month or 13 $50,000 leads a month.

acquisition_channels.details: Cold outreach to business owners; the specific outreach method is not stated.

ideas.delivery: Build and optimize websites with Ready, then set up integrations and appointment or payment flows for clients.
ideas.other_uk_rules: The outreach method is unspecified. In the UK, unsolicited electronic marketing to sole traders is restricted; cold email should be limited to corporate subscribers with an opt-out, and cold calls should screen TPS/CTPS. UK GDPR applies to prospect data. The suggested monthly fee is B2B; DMCC Act subscription rules may matter if the offer is adapted for consumers.
